records.claim: Remark 2.2(i)
records.quote: Remark 2.2 (i) The over-assessment and under-assessment of a reliability function (say SF, FR, RFR, MRL, AI) are basically the study of the stochastic ordering (respectively, usual stochastic order, FR order, RFR order, MRL order, AI order, respectively) among the corresponding function between the dependent and independent counterpart of the system concerned. Mathematically, we express as, let TD and TI represent the lifetime of the series system formed by n dependent and independent components respectively. Clearly, TD ≤ST (≥ST)TI if and only if there is OA (UA) in SF. So is for orders based on FR, MRL, RFR, AI, i.e., TD ≤FR (≥FR)TI if and only if there is UA (OA) in FR., TD ≤MRL (≥MRL)TI if and only if there is OA (UA) in MRL., TD ≤RFR (≥RFR)TI if and only if there is OA (UA) in RFR., TD ≤AI (≥AI)TI if and only if there is UA (OA) in AI.
